CBRS.headline: Semiconductor Stocks Are Sinking. These 2 AI Chip Stocks Could Make You Richer on the Rebound.
CBRS.description: While semiconductor stocks have fallen sharply (down 40% from June highs), two AI chip companies—Cerebras and Arm Holdings—reported strong quarterly results that suggest potential for rebound gains. Cerebras raised 2026 forecasts, beat profit expectations, and added Microsoft as a customer, while Arm's data center royalties doubled and it now commands over 50% of servers at major cloud companies.

CRDO.headline: Credo's Optical Expansion: Can It Gain Ground Against Rivals?
CRDO.description: Credo Technology (CRDO) is capitalizing on AI-driven demand for optical connectivity solutions, expecting optical revenues to exceed $600 million in fiscal 2027. The company's optical DSP business posted record Q1 revenues, with ZeroFlap Optics, silicon photonics PICs, and optical DSPs each projected to contribute over $100 million. INSM.headline: AGIO Stock Rises 8.4%: Is a Buyout on the Cards Post SNY/INSM Deal?
INSM.description: Agios Pharmaceuticals shares surged 8.4% following Sanofi's $41 billion acquisition of Insmed, reviving hopes for biotech M&A activity. The company's strong position in rare blood disorders, particularly with mitapivat's potential expansion into sickle cell disease, positions it as a potential acquisition target for major pharmaceutical companies. Pyrukynd and Aqvesme sales grew 255% to $120.9 million in the first nine months of 2026.

INSM.headline: Is Sanofi's $41B Buyout of Insmed a Strategic Fit?
INSM.description: Sanofi has agreed to acquire U.S.-based Insmed for $41 billion ($175 per share in cash), marking the largest pharmaceutical transaction of 2026. The deal adds respiratory medicines Brinsupri and Arikayce to Sanofi's portfolio, along with late-stage candidate TPIP in development for multiple pulmonary indications. The acquisition is expected to close in H1 2027 and be accretive to EPS by end of 2028, supporting Sanofi's strategy to secure growth beyond Dupixent's loss of exclusivity.

INSM.headline: Communiqué de presse : Sanofi va acquérir Insmed, une étape stratégique qui renforce son avenir à long terme
INSM.description: Sanofi announced the acquisition of Insmed Incorporated for $175 per share ($41 billion total) to strengthen its position in respiratory diseases and rare immunological conditions. The deal includes two commercialized products (Brinsupri and Arikayce) and a promising Phase 3 pipeline program (TPIP). The acquisition is expected to be accretive to earnings by end of 2028 and is targeted to close in H1 2027.

INSM.headline: Press Release: Sanofi to acquire Insmed in strategic step that strengthens long-term future
INSM.description: Sanofi announced an agreement to acquire Insmed Incorporated for $175 per share ($41.0 billion) to strengthen its respiratory disease portfolio and immunology capabilities. The acquisition includes two commercialized products—Brinsupri and Arikayce—and a promising phase 3 pipeline asset. The transaction is expected to be EPS accretive by end of 2028 and close in H1 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and shareholder approval.

MTSI.headline: Here's Why M/A-Com (MTSI) Is a Great 'Buy the Bottom' Stock Now
MTSI.description: M/A-Com (MTSI) has formed a hammer chart pattern after a 5% decline over four weeks, signaling potential trend reversal. The stock is supported by strong fundamental indicators including a 15.2% upward revision in consensus EPS estimates over the last 30 days and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) rating, suggesting improved company prospects.

KYMR.headline: Kymera Shares Soar 30% After Positive Atopic Dermatitis Drug Data
KYMR.description: Kymera Therapeutics announced positive results from its BROADEN2 phase IIb trial of KT-621, an investigational oral STAT6 degrader for moderate to severe atopic dermatitis. The mid-dose group achieved a 72% EASI reduction versus 27% for placebo, with significant itch relief and rapid onset of activity. The company plans to advance into phase III development by mid-2027, with potential to compete against established biologics like Dupixent.

KYMR.headline: Kymera Therapeutics Announces Pricing of Upsized $1.75 Billion Public Offering
KYMR.description: Kymera Therapeutics priced an underwritten public offering of $1.75 billion, selling 11.64 million shares at $150.37 per share. The clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company plans to use net proceeds to advance its pipeline of oral small molecule degrader programs for immunological diseases. The offering is expected to close on November 25, 2026.

KYMR.headline: Kymera Therapeutics Announces Proposed Public Offering
KYMR.description: Kymera Therapeutics, a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, announced an underwritten public offering of $1.5 billion in common stock, with an additional $225 million option for underwriters. The company plans to use proceeds to advance its pipeline of targeted protein degradation (TPD) degrader programs for immunological diseases and general corporate purposes.

MRVL.headline: Broadcom vs. Qualcomm: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
MRVL.description: Broadcom and Qualcomm represent two different paths in the semiconductor industry. Broadcom is focused on AI infrastructure and data centers with projected revenue doubling to $230 billion by 2027, while Qualcomm dominates mobile connectivity but faces headwinds in its core handset business. Despite similar forward P/E ratios, Broadcom's stronger growth trajectory and AI exposure make it the recommended buy for 2027, though both companies carry concentration risks with major customers.

MRVL.headline: Can MXL's AI Data Center Business Sustain Its Strong Growth Momentum?
MRVL.description: MaxLinear's AI data center business is experiencing strong growth with Q3 revenues up 72% year-over-year and infrastructure revenues surging 210%. The company raised its 2026 optical data center revenue outlook to $250-$270 million, driven by adoption of its Keystone and upcoming Rushmore products. However, MaxLinear faces supply constraints and stiff competition from Marvell and Broadcom in the high-speed optical connectivity market.

MRVL.description: Marvell Technology stock declined 9.1% to $131.57, significantly underperforming the S&P 500's 0.5% loss. SK Hynix stock remains attractively priced at less than 7 times earnings, though concerns persist about maintaining profit margins amid AI market volatility.

UMC.headline: TSM's AI-Driven Growth Accelerates: Is There More Upside Ahead?
UMC.description: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM) reported Q3 2026 revenues of $46.72 billion, up 41.2% year-over-year, driven by strong AI infrastructure demand. HPC contributed 68% of revenues, while 2-nanometer technology reached 8% of wafer sales. TSM expects full-year 2026 revenue growth of 44% and plans to more than double N2 capacity in 2027. Competitors UMC and Intel also reported strong performance, with UMC's revenues up 25.6% and Intel's Data Center and AI revenues surging 78%.

While Nvidia maintains 75% market share in AI accelerators, competitors' custom chips are gaining traction for agentic AI tasks, and Nvidia's gross margins are declining from competitive pressure.

The promotion follows iPronics' Series B funding of $125 million and expansion into Santa Clara, California.

NVDA.description: Nvidia has brought back Jensen Huang as CEO, triggering a significant stock sell-off. Historical analysis suggests that only 11 of 2,133 weeks since 1986 experienced sell-offs as severe as the current one, indicating this downturn could present a buying opportunity for investors.

NVDA.description: Billionaire hedge fund manager David Tepper completely exited his AMD position in Q3 while making Micron Technology his largest holding at 17.5% of his portfolio. NVDA.headline: The Numbers Behind Your Stocks' Wild Swings
NVDA.description: Individual stocks are experiencing extreme volatility far exceeding overall market swings, with the VIXEQ (individual stock volatility index) at 57.91 versus VIX at 35.89. Three factors drive this: surging options trading (70-90 million contracts daily), leveraged single-stock ETFs accounting for 8-9% of trading volume, and increased passive investing reducing available shares. While alarming, long-term investors should focus on business fundamentals rather than daily price movements.

MU.description: Micron Technology stock has pulled back 39% since July 2026 despite strong fundamentals, presenting a buying opportunity according to the analyst. MU.headline: Micron Reports in December. Here's the 1 Number I'll Be Watching.
MU.description: Micron Technology will report Q1 fiscal 2027 results on December 17. The key metric to watch is the fiscal Q2 revenue guidance, which will indicate whether memory chip prices are still rising or have stalled. The stock has fallen 42% from its September peak despite being up 120% for 2026. A guidance increase of only ~5% would suggest prices have stopped climbing, while a larger increase would indicate continued price momentum driven by AI demand.
